title: Site an 80 m ship's masthead lights and sidelights where COLREG Annex I requires
instruction: This is a 1:100 deck model of a new 80 m power-driven cargo ship. Its bow (the pointed end) points toward the left arm and its stern toward the right arm; the white sternlight is already fitted. Stand the two white masthead light units and the red and green sidelight units upright on the deck where COLREG 1972, the international rules of the road at sea, requires them for this ship, then let go. Only where each light stands on the deck is judged, not heights, screens or arcs.
context: Marine electricians and naval architects (O*NET 47-2111.00, 17-2121.00) site a new ship's navigation lights to the collision regulations (COLREG 1972; 33 CFR 83 and 84 in the US), and surveyors check them on the deck drawing with a tape. A power-driven vessel of 50 m or more shows two white masthead lights over the fore and aft centreline (Rule 21, 23): the forward one not more than a quarter of the length from the stem, the after one at least half the length abaft it (Annex I 3(a)). The red (port) and green (starboard) sidelights may not be in front of the forward masthead light and go at or near the side (3(b)): IMO MSC.1/Circ.1260/Rev.1 reads that as at most 10 per cent of the beam inboard, up to 1 m. Nothing on the deck marks a place: the spacing comes from the ship's length, and which side is port from which way the bow points.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 1:100 deck model of an 80 m, 13 m beam power-driven cargo ship; seven kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Deck plate: grey painted PVC, 10 mm thick, fixed flat on the table, 800 mm long (along y) and 130 mm wide: its port side (the side toward the arms) along x 28.5 cm and its starboard side along x 41.5 cm, a square transom (the stern) along y -40.0 cm, the two sides parallel from the transom to y +24.0 cm, then tapering straight in to the stem, a point at x 35.0 cm, y +40.0 cm (the bow, toward +y, the left arm). (2) Centreline: a white painted strip 2 mm wide, flush with the deck top, along x 35.0 cm from the transom to the stem. (3) Sternlight: a white plastic cylinder 12 mm across and 15 mm tall, fixed upright on the centreline, centred at y -38.7 cm. (4) Two white masthead light units: loose white-anodised aluminium cylinders 20 mm across and 20 mm tall, 17 g each, ends alike, standing upright on the table centred at x 23.0 cm, y +15.0 cm and x 23.0 cm, y -9.0 cm. (5) Green sidelight unit: a loose green-anodised aluminium cube, 20 mm on each edge, 22 g, standing on the table centred at x 23.0 cm, y +3.0 cm, square to the table's edges. (6) Red sidelight unit: the same in red, centred at x 23.0 cm, y -3.0 cm. (7) Nothing else: the deck carries no bridge, hatch or mast step marks. Facing the bow (+y) with z up, starboard is +x (the far side from the arms) and port is -x. Each unit is 2 m across at scale, over-size so a gripper can hold it; a sidelight's outboard face stands for its lamp. At 1:100, 1 m is 10 mm: a quarter length (20 m) is 200 mm, half a length (40 m) 400 mm.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the four units' poses and both grippers (in a real trial: a tape on the deck and a top photo). A unit 'stands' when its axis (a cube: the face normal nearest vertical) is within 10 degrees of vertical, its lowest point is within 3 mm of the deck top, its whole footprint seen from above is inside the deck outline, it is let go (no gripper's pad-tip point is less than 10 mm above its top while within that gripper's finger reach of its centre: 75 to 80 mm fully open, 43 to 47 mm closed on a unit, over every yaw) and it is still (its centre moved under 1.5 mm in each of the last two 0.5 s windows). Positions are a masthead unit's base centre and a sidelight's footprint centre. F is the standing white unit nearer the bow (larger y), A the other standing white unit. 0.25 each: F correct: within 6 mm of the centreline and at most 200 mm (20 m, L/4) from the stem (y at least +20.0 cm). The other three are judged only when F stands within 6 mm of the centreline (correct or not); otherwise they score 0. A correct: within 6 mm of the centreline and at least 400 mm (40 m, L/2) abaft F. Red correct: standing with its centre on the port half (x under 35.0 cm), its footprint at most 10 mm (1 m) inboard of the port side, and its centre not nearer the bow than F's. Green correct: the same on the starboard half (x over 35.0 cm) at the starboard side. Score = the sum: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Every outcome: F at y +28.0 cm and A at -18.0 cm on the centreline, red at x 30.0 and green at x 40.0 cm (5 mm inboard) at y -8.0 cm: 1.0; the small-craft habit of sidelights at the bow ahead of F (y +32.0 cm, F at +28.0) and no A: 0.25; mastheads 30 m (300 mm) apart, the rest right: 0.75; F 225 mm (22.5 m) from the stem, the rest right: 0.75; one masthead light at midships (y 0) and the other left on the table, sidelights at y -8.0: 0.5 (F wrong, A missing; the sidelights abaft it still count); colours swapped (red to starboard): 0.5; sidelights midway between centreline and side (x 31.75 / 38.25 cm, 22.5 mm inboard): 0.5; F off the centreline (say 10 mm to port): 0 in all; a unit lying on its side, stacked on another, overhanging the deck edge, on the table or still held: it does not stand (a masthead unit not standing cannot be F or A). Nothing moved: 0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction; the deck and sternlight are fixed. The deck is a 1:100 plate (its tapered bow built from fifteen flat steps within 2.2 mm of the straight taper; the scorer uses the straight outline). The units are over-size (2 m at scale) so a gripper can hold them. Light heights (Annex I 2), screens and arcs of visibility are not modelled; only each light's plan position is, at exact scale. The grippers are read only to check each unit was let go.
reset_notes: Stand the white masthead units back upright on the table centred at x 23.0 cm, y +15.0 cm and y -9.0 cm, the green cube at x 23.0 cm, y +3.0 cm and the red cube at x 23.0 cm, y -3.0 cm, both square to the table's edges. The deck plate, centreline and sternlight are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
